content: Ceftriaxone for injection is strictly contraindicated in patients who have a known hypersensitivity or allergy to cephalosporin-class antibiotics. Neonates, defined as infants aged 28 days or younger, who are hyperbilirubinemic, particularly those born prematurely, must not be treated with ceftriaxone for injection. This is due to in vitro evidence demonstrating that ceftriaxone can displace bilirubin from its binding sites on serum albumin, potentially increasing the risk of bilirubin encephalopathy in these patients. Ceftriaxone for injection is also contraindicated in neonates who require, or are anticipated to require, treatment with calcium-containing intravenous solutions, including continuous calcium-containing infusions such as parenteral nutrition. This is because of the risk of precipitation of ceftriaxone-calcium complexes, which can have serious clinical consequences. There have been reports of fatal outcomes in neonates who received ceftriaxone for injection in conjunction with calcium-containing fluids. In these cases, crystalline material was observed in the lungs and kidneys during autopsy. In some instances, the same intravenous infusion line was used for both ceftriaxone and calcium-containing fluids, and precipitates were noted in the infusion line. At least one fatality has been reported in a neonate who received ceftriaxone and calcium-containing fluids at different times through separate intravenous lines. In this case, no crystalline material was observed during autopsy. It is important to note that such adverse events have not been reported in patients outside the neonatal population.
